title: Think before you post

cards.text: The FTC says you cannot fully control who sees a post, even with privacy settings. A post can be saved and shared.
cards.line: Once it is out, it may travel far.

cards.text: Use privacy settings to limit who can see your posts and where you are. The FTC says to stop and think before you post.
cards.line: Check who can see it first.

cards.text: Keep personal details out of your profile and posts. The FDIC says birthdates, pets' names, and addresses can help crooks guess your passwords.
cards.line: Some details belong only to you.

checks.prompt: What can happen after you post something online?
options: It can be saved and shared
It disappears once you delete it
checks.answer: It can be saved and shared
checks.why: The FTC says a deleted post could be saved, shared, and live online.

checks.prompt: What should you check before posting?
options: How many people liked your last post
checks.why: The FTC says to find out how to turn on privacy settings for devices, apps, and social accounts.

checks.prompt: Which detail is best kept off a public post?
options: A book you enjoyed this year
checks.why: The FDIC says to keep details like your address and birthday out of online profiles and posts.

takeaway: Pause before posting. Keep personal details private.

sources.name: FDIC, protect your finances and identity online

situations.text: If you delete a post, no one can have saved or shared it.
situations.why: The FTC says a deleted post could be saved, shared, and live online.

situations.text: You post your home address and birthday on your public profile.
situations.why: The FDIC says to keep details like these out of online profiles and posts.

situations.text: Should you check your privacy settings before you post?
situations.why: The FTC says to use privacy settings and stop and think before you post.
